<description>
This is a simple mempool PR that fixes #33510.

Evicting mempool transactions by age (`-mempoolexpiry`, default two weeks) is
incentive-incompatible: it may drop transactions that could still be mined
As discussed IRL and in #33510, this PR hence removes age-based eviction entirely.

Transactions now leave the mempool only via size limiting (`-maxmempool`),
replacement, conflicts, or inclusion in a block. The `EXPIRY` removal reason is
dropped. `-mempoolexpiry` is retained as a hidden no-op that warns when set, so
existing configurations keep starting.

Nice side effects:
- With expiry gone, the `entry_time` index has no readers. Removing it saves an
  ordered-tree node per mempool entry and drops a now unused Boost
  include.
- The `DynamicMemoryUsage()` per-entry estimate drops from three indexes to
  two, so within the same `-maxmempool` budget the mempool fits slightly more
  transactions.
</description>

<commits>
8d4b1abbec test: stop relying on mempool expiry in tests

Rework the tests that exercise time-based mempool expiry so they no
longer depend on it, before the feature is removed: trigger
mempool:removed via RBF in the USDT test, check chain rebroadcast via
peer invs in the wallet resend test, and drop the expiry knobs from the
mempool fuzz targets.

d40e511d9d mempool: remove time-based transaction expiry

Evicting transactions purely by age (-mempoolexpiry, default two weeks)
is incentive-incompatible: it can drop still-mineable transactions, such
as a low-feerate parent waiting on a fee-bumping child. Remove it;
-mempoolexpiry is kept as a no-op that warns when set.

1556184fbd mempool: remove now-unused entry_time index and includes

Expire() was the entry_time index's only user; drop the index, its tag
and comparator, and the boost headers only it needed. Also tidy includes:
move util/time.h into txmempool.h, drop <chrono>/<memory> from
mempool_args.cpp, and remove the now-unused identity.hpp from
EXPECTED_BOOST_INCLUDES.
</commits>
